title: Technical Information Operations Officer (I) (LtCol to 2ndLt) FMOS, DC I
raw_text:
10. MOS 8834, Technical Information Operations Officer (I) (LtCol to 2ndLt)
FMOS, DC I

    a. Summary. Technical Information Operations (IO) Officers identify,
describe, and apply concepts, theories, and practices associated with the
employment of information across the range of military operations. These
officers develop and support information DOTMLPF solutions as part of the
requirements or acquisitions process. Officers will also plan, coordinate,
execute and assess IO on MAGTFs.

    b. Prerequisites.       Security requirement:   TS/SCI security clearance
eligibility.

       c.   Requirements

        (1) Complete the Information Warfare (IW) curriculum, number 595 at
the Naval Postgraduate School, Monterey, CA. In accomplishing this, the
officer must have:

                (a) Earned a master's degree in information warfare systems
engineering.

                (b) Completed a thesis on a topic relating to information
operations.

        (2) Graduate must have a solid understanding of the Marine Corps
planning process in order to participate in technical IO planning as part of
the MAGTF Command Element (CE) staff.

       d.   Duties

        (1) Plans, supervises, coordinates and executes research, design,
development, and testing of information concepts, and information related
systems and equipment.

        (2) Monitors technological developments in the information field to
ensure planning reflects future systems development and prepares procurement
plans and programs for information related systems and equipment.




                                         1-352                        Enclosure (1)
 1147                                                               NAVMC 1200.1L



        (3) Assists in the development of information policy to guide
commands in the development of strategy, doctrine, and systems procurement.

        (4) Develops Information doctrine that allows for the development of
plans, education and training in the conduct of information.

        (5) Advises the commanding officer, operations officer, and the
information working group lead on the technical aspects of information in
order to provide integrated, synchronized, and coordinated effects in the
information environment to achieve an operational advantage for the
commander.

        (6) Serve as a subject matter expert and staff planner for MAGTF
information working groups in the fields of electronic warfare and
information operations.

       e.   Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code

            (1) Electronics Engineers, Except Computer 17-2072.

            (2) Electrical Engineers 17-2071.

       f.   Related Military Skill

            (1) Advanced Information Operations Planner, 0550.

            (2) Basic Information Planner, 1781.

            (3) Special Technical Operations Officer, 8016.

matches: Analyze organizational, occupational, and industrial data to facilitate organizational functions and provide technical information to business, industry, and government.
Technical Information Operations (IO) Officers identify, describe, and apply concepts, theories, and practices associated with the employment of information across the range of military operations.
Analyze acquisitions to ensure conformance with strategic goals or regulatory requirements.
These officers develop and support information DOTMLPF solutions as part of the requirements or acquisitions process.
Write reports, maintain research information, or perform clerical duties.
d. Duties (1) Plans, supervises, coordinates and executes research, design, development, and testing of information concepts, and information related systems and equipment.

Develop or update project plans for information technology projects including information such as project objectives, technologies, systems, information specifications, schedules, funding, and staffing.

(2) Monitors technological developments in the information field to ensure planning reflects future systems development and prepares procurement plans and programs for information related systems and equipment.
Develop policies or requirements for data collection, processing, or reporting.
(3) Assists in the development of information policy to guide commands in the development of strategy, doctrine, and systems procurement.
Provide information to the public by leading workshops and training programs and by developing educational materials.
(4) Develops Information doctrine that allows for the development of plans, education and training in the conduct of information.
Confer with engineering, supervisory, or manufacturing personnel to exchange technical information.

(5) Advises the commanding officer, operations officer, and the information working group lead on the technical aspects of information in order to provide integrated, synchronized, and coordinated effects in the information environment to achieve an operational advantage for the commander.
Operate electronic mail systems and coordinate the flow of information, internally or with other organizations.
(6) Serve as a subject matter expert and staff planner for MAGTF information working groups in the fields of electronic warfare and information operations.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
